explanation: Sealed in, she moults her flight feathers and raises the chicks while the male feeds the family through the gap. The wall keeps out snakes and monkeys.

claims.text: In many hornbill species the female seals herself into a tree-hole nest with mud, droppings or food, leaving a narrow slit through which the male passes food.
Toucans, woodpeckers and kingfishers do not wall the female into the nest.
Many sealed-in female hornbills moult their flight feathers while nesting.
The sealed entrance protects the nest from predators such as snakes and monkeys.
